newsitem.title: USA: Geneva Steel sees Q4 hurt by imports.
newsitem.headline: Geneva Steel sees Q4 hurt by imports.

text.p: Geneva Steel Co said on Monday that imports of cut-to-length carbon plate steel will adversely affect the company's fourth quarter results.

The company and other domestic steel makers had filed anti-dumping petitions with the U.S. Department of Commerce and International Trade Commission against the Russian Federation, Ukraine, China and South Africa on November 5, 1996.

Geneva Steel said it was difficult to determine how much the imports would hurt its results in the fourth quarter of the calendar year, but they would fall short of the company's earlier expectations.

A Geneva Steel spokesman said "people in the market" were expecting the company's performance to be similar to its performance in three months ended September 30. For the period, it reported a profit of $0.05 a share on sales of $203.3 million. The company's fiscal year ends in September.
In August, plate imports accounted for 30 percent of the U.S. market on an annualized basis, and data showed the trend extending into September, Geneva said.
The imports led to lower prices and shortened order books, Geneva said.
In response, the company cut employees' working hours. The reduction was the equivalent of laying off about 185 workers, the company said.
